title: Compact routing context and async fallback queue refactor
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Context: The current smart routing stack accumulates a fairly large per-request context object during policy evaluation and fallback coordination. This causes increased GC/alloc churn, higher p99 latency in high-concurrency paths, and complex lock interactions when regions and fallback adapters are consulted. Goal: shrink the routing context to a compact, immutable snapshot for the routing hotpath and replace the synchronous fallback queue with an async bounded channel + backpressure strategy. Deliverables: 1) CompactRoutingContext: immutable, pre-computed routing metadata (region affinity, model-compatibility bitflags, capacity hints) that can be cheaply cloned across goroutines/tasks. 2) AsyncFallbackQueue: bounded async queue for fallback candidates with configurable backpressure and timeout semantics to avoid head-of-line blocking. 3) Compatibility shim and Canary rollout plan enabled by feature flag `routing_v2`. 4) Updated metrics and tracing spans covering fallback decisions and queue backpressure events. Why now: we saw a 1.8x increase in p99 latency under bursty traffic in US regions during recent load tests. This refactor reduces critical-path locking and will enable future kernel-level improvements and caching optimizations.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for CompactRoutingContext serialization/clone behavior
E2E test validating fallback ordering and bounded queue behavior under contention
Benchmarks show >=15% p99 latency reduction and 10-20% CPU reduction on the routing hotpath in canary region
Feature flag `routing_v2` toggles behavior and has automated rollout/rollback in the console
No regression in end-to-end correctness (requests still resolve to identical final model/routing decisions within tolerances)
